title: Ambivalence in the Context of Competing Narratives: Exploration Through a Case of the US Military Base Issue in Okinawa
materials_method: Survey of 172 Okinawan participants; exploratory factor analysis; latent profile analysis; mapping narrative profiles, behavioral responses, and social positions
main_finding: Dominant and resistance narratives were often endorsed together; narrative profiles were significantly related to behavioral responses
project_relationship: Rejects a simple pro-/anti-US binary; supports keeping legitimation claims separate from behavior and measuring ambivalence
verification_note: University repository record and DOI verified; do not reuse an internal subgroup percentage as if it described the full N=172

title: 沖縄軍人妻の研究
materials_method: Cultural-anthropological fieldwork on U.S. Marine bases in Okinawa and surrounding communities; family support systems; community interaction; nine participant profiles
main_finding: Military-family life, support institutions, spouse networks, good-neighbor activities, and local interaction reproduce an everyday social world around the bases while also containing conflict and ambivalence
project_relationship: Direct basis for treating spouse clubs, family services, and community contact as organizational infrastructure; does not prove their political effect
verification_note: Publisher page, contents, ISBN 9784876982370, and issue date 2012-11 verified

title: ‘We are Okinawans but of a different kind’: New/old social movements and the U.S. Military in Okinawa
materials_method: Ethnographic analysis of the offshore-base dispute after the 1995 rape and of relations among movement agendas and participants
main_finding: Okinawan mobilization combines historical continuity with contemporary diversity across ecology, peace, women, and human-rights agendas; class and material conditions remain central
project_relationship: Issue diversification is established scholarship; the database can add longitudinal actor, role, and relation evidence rather than claim discovery of diversity
verification_note: University research portal and DOI verified

title: Dugong v. Rumsfeld: social movements and the construction of ecological security
materials_method: Comparative qualitative analysis of the Okinawa dugong and Jeju Gureombi as nonhuman movement symbols using movement and public materials
main_finding: Movement actors constructed ecological security and turned local struggles into transnational causes, although symbolic resonance and diffusion were partial
project_relationship: The project can reconstruct the actor-role-venue-output pathway and compare institutional outcomes; environmental translation itself is not a new finding
verification_note: SAGE article page and DOI verified

title: Base Towns: Local Contestation of the U.S. Military in Korea and Japan
materials_method: Fieldwork interviews, participant observation, and protest-event data for 20 U.S. bases in Korea and Japan, 2000–2015
main_finding: Broad mobilization becomes possible when activists politicize quotidian disruption with locally resonant frames and local political allies; some strategies can also reinforce the presumed inevitability of U.S. presence
project_relationship: Makes local-damage framing and local political mediation prior findings; database contribution is organizational infrastructure, comparison, and typed mechanisms
verification_note: Oxford Academic book page and DOI verified

title: Activists, Alliances, and Anti-U.S. Base Protests
materials_method: Comparative case studies across the Philippines, Japan/Okinawa, Ecuador, Italy, and Korea; interviews with activists, politicians, and base officials
main_finding: Movement networks affect mobilization, but protest outcomes depend heavily on elite and alliance security consensus
project_relationship: Supports modeling movement coalitions together with institutional constraints and avoiding a network-only explanation of base outcomes
verification_note: Cambridge book page, contents, and DOI verified

title: No Bases? Assessing the Impact of Social Movements Challenging US Foreign Military Bases
materials_method: Seventeen years of multi-country research including participant observation, archives, and interviews in 14 countries and territories
main_finding: Base movements can affect operations, deployments, political-economic relations, people, and other movements even when bases do not close; many pursue accountability and harm reduction rather than categorical anti-Americanism
project_relationship: Justifies an outcome ladder including disclosure, review, compensation, delay, and operating costs instead of a closure-only measure
verification_note: Publisher full-text page and DOI verified

title: Transnational Identities on Okinawa’s Military Bases: Invisible Armies
materials_method: Ethnographic research on civilian USFJ employees, migration, identity, ethnicity, nationality, and capital, including Okinawan and Philippine-heritage returnees
main_finding: The base is reproduced through civilian labor and transnational migration as well as through military personnel
project_relationship: Defines an important boundary: an NGO database captures only part of garrison reproduction and should identify labor/migration nodes as contextual or future layers
verification_note: Springer book page and DOI verified

title: Intimacy across the Fencelines: Sex, Marriage, and the U.S. Military in Okinawa
materials_method: Ethnographic and narrative analysis of U.S. service members and Okinawan spouses and families across race, gender, class, and military-civilian boundaries
main_finding: Marriage, family, and intimacy are constitutive interfaces between the garrison and Okinawan society, not merely private background
project_relationship: Shows why public person-role links can be informative but why family relations require privacy and scope safeguards
verification_note: Cornell Scholarship Online book page and DOI verified

authors: Michael A. Allen; Michael E. Flynn; Carla Martinez Machain; Andrew Stravers
title: Outside the Wire: U.S. Military Deployments and Public Opinion in Host States
materials_method: Cross-national survey data from 14 countries hosting U.S. forces
main_finding: Contact with U.S. personnel and perceived economic benefits are associated with more favorable views of U.S. presence, people, and government
project_relationship: Provides a testable legitimation-mechanism hypothesis; the organization database can measure exposure infrastructure but not infer attitude effects
verification_note: Cambridge journal page and DOI verified; association is not an Okinawa-specific causal estimate

authors: Takako Hikotani; Yusaku Horiuchi; Atsushi Tago
title: Revisiting negative externalities of US military bases: the case of Okinawa
materials_method: Two pre-registered surveys fielded in August 2020: Japan national sample N=994 and Okinawa sample N=319; descriptive comparison and regression analysis
main_finding: Okinawans have more contact and network benefits yet remain considerably more negative about bases concentrated in Okinawa, regardless of contact and economic benefits
project_relationship: Directly blocks any inference that service or contact automatically legitimates the local military presence; motivates recipient and attitude evidence
verification_note: Oxford journal page, samples, publication history, and DOI verified; online publication 2022, issue year 2023

title: Not Seeing the Forest for the Helicopters: UNESCO Recognition and Resistance to the US Military in Okinawa
materials_method: Interviews conducted 2019–2023 and other primary-source research on Yambaru activists and UNESCO recognition
main_finding: Activists used Japan’s UNESCO nomination to expose military impacts and gain disclosure and an international channel, without securing removal or cessation
project_relationship: Offers a second international environmental pathway beyond the dugong case and a clean intermediate-outcome comparison

title: The United States’ Public Diplomacy and Psychological Warfare under the Jurisdiction
publication: Academic Archives of Yamaguchi Prefectural University 15:235–248
materials_method: Historical policy analysis of Eisenhower-era U.S. Okinawa policy, the National Security Council, Pentagon, and civilian-agency coordination
main_finding: U.S. authorities institutionalized public diplomacy and psychological-warfare coordination to counter anti-U.S. sentiment in occupied Okinawa
project_relationship: Establishes a historical state strategy and suggests fields for public-diplomacy records; it is pre-1972 context, not evidence about current NGOs
verification_note: University repository version of record, issue date, pages, and ISSN verified

title: CIA: How to shape Okinawan public opinion on the U.S. military presence
publication: The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus 16(13), Article 4
materials_method: Document analysis of a 2012 CIA Open Source Center manual released under FOIA
main_finding: U.S. analysts explicitly mapped Okinawan master narratives and public-opinion dynamics surrounding the military presence
project_relationship: Supports collecting official narrative-management documents and coding legitimation claims; does not establish public-opinion effects
verification_note: Cambridge journal metadata page and DOI verified

title: Social Movements and Networks: Relational Approaches to Collective Action
materials_method: Relational approaches to recruitment, interpersonal networks, interorganizational networks, brokerage, diffusion, and network evolution
main_finding: Social movements are better explained through relational structures and changing ties than through actor attributes alone
project_relationship: Supports separate person–organization, organization–event, and interorganizational layers with temporal brokerage
verification_note: Oxford Academic book page and DOI verified

title: The Cement of Civil Society: Studying Networks in Localities
materials_method: Comparative fieldwork on civic organizations in Glasgow and Bristol combined with social-movement and network theory
main_finding: Modes of coordination and interorganizational relations cut across rigid distinctions such as service versus protest and formal versus grassroots organization
project_relationship: Core methodological warrant for coding mechanisms and multiplex positions instead of assigning whole organizations to pro-/anti-base camps
verification_note: Cambridge book page and DOI verified

title: The Integrative Power of Civic Networks
materials_method: Comparative analysis of civic collaboration networks in Glasgow and Bristol
main_finding: Dense identity-based clusters can be linked by a smaller number of instrumental transactions, producing polycentric coordination
project_relationship: Provides a test for Okinawa: identify typed clusters and cross-layer brokers rather than infer integration from co-signing
verification_note: Publisher journal page and DOI verified

title: Effects of missing data in social networks
materials_method: Simulation studies using bipartite networks and scientific-collaboration data to examine boundary specification, missing actors/affiliations, and fixed-choice effects
main_finding: Network statistics can change substantially under missing actors, affiliations, and sampling boundaries
project_relationship: Requires source-deletion, no-website-actor, identity-uncertainty, and unobserved-person/recipient sensitivity before claiming centrality or separation
verification_note: Publisher article page and DOI verified
